title: UN Women AI School
summary: UN Women’s AI School has participants use ChatGPT, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot and build custom GPTs for research and advocacy; no source measures what the AI changed.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Participants in the UN Women AI School use ChatGPT, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot for research, knowledge products, content creation and advocacy. Activities include developing custom GPTs for policy briefs, proposals and other work. The program links to custom GPTs for humanitarian work, technology-facilitated gender-based violence and women’s empowerment principles. UN Women reports that young leaders from the 30 for 2030 network built a custom GPT for the Beijing+30 review with the AI School and showed it at the ministerial conference in Bangkok on 19 November 2024. UN Women opened the 2025 edition as an online program on 5 March 2025. In the ITU account, current as of June 2025, the project team reports attendance and satisfaction for the overall program. The team does not measure the effect of AI on learning or workplace performance. No evaluation of what participants learned or produced with AI had been published by October 2026.
purpose: Use generative AI in practical learning, research, knowledge management and advocacy work.
